activities.anchor: Every robot runs the same inner cycle
activities.caption: rebuild the control stack, reflex to reasoning
activities.name: rbeLoopOrder

config.prompt: The stack runs bottom-up at different frequencies — order the layers:
items: low-level joint control — the servo loop corrects torque every millisecond
state estimation — fusing encoders, IMUs and vision into one belief about position
motion planning — searching configuration space for a collision-free path
the integrator makes the stack fail gracefully — e-stops, watchdogs, velocity limits
config.why: Each layer's failure modes are distinct: hardware fails, sensors lie, planners hit local minima — and a walking robot must adjust roughly every 10 milliseconds, two orders of magnitude faster than a datacentre prompt.

activities.anchor: A mobile robot's founding problem is the chicken-and-egg
activities.caption: pair each SLAM piece with its role
activities.name: rbeSlamMatch

config.prompt: Building the map while walking it — pair each piece with its role:

pairs.right: you cannot map without knowing where you are, and cannot localise without a map
poses and landmarks as nodes, sensor observations as constraints, least squares finding the best explanation
recognising a previously seen place, snapping accumulated drift shut
the 4-to-24-minute signal delay makes teleoperation a non-starter — autonomy is the only way the mission moves

config.why: The descendant technology is everywhere: robot vacuums, warehouse AMRs, AR headsets — and Mars rovers, where local estimation is the backbone.

activities.caption: true or false — the satellite assumption
activities.name: rbeGpsJudge

statements.s: GPS is unavailable indoors and degraded in urban canyons.
statements.why: And centimetre-accurate only with expensive augmentation — which is why it is not the backbone.
Every serious mobile robot treats satellite positioning as one optional input; SLAM-style local estimation is the backbone.
One more reason local estimation from the robot's own sensors carries the load.
No GPS at all on Mars — Perseverance navigates with AutoNav instead.

activities.caption: file the routes to robot skill
activities.name: rbeSkillBuckets

config.prompt: Three routes to robot skill — file each fact:

items.label: record human teleoperation, train a policy mapping observations to actions, deploy
covariate shift — the robot drifts into states the demonstrator never visited
model the distribution of good actions and sample from it — two valid grasps both survive
handles multimodal tasks that regression averages into failure
transformers pretrained on internet-scale vision and language, fine-tuned on robot trajectories
RT-2 generalised to objects and instructions never demonstrated

config.why: The data bottleneck defines the field: the internet has billions of labelled images but almost no labelled actions — hence teleop fleets and Open X-Embodiment's 22 robot types.

activities.anchor: Deployment follows value per movement and tolerance for chaos.
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the installed fleet
activities.name: rbeFleetEstimate

config.prompt: About how many industrial robots are installed worldwide, per the International Federation of Robotics?
config.why: About 4 million industrial arms installed worldwide — alongside Amazon's roughly 750,000 mobile robots: structured environments won first.
config.context: Waymo crossed 100,000 paid rides per week in 2024 — real and impressive, and fifteen years late against the original promise.

activities.anchor: robots fail because their AI is bad
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the uptime diagnosis
activities.name: rbeUptimeSpot

config.prompt: This deployment post-mortem contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Diagnostics usually rank sensor degradation, actuator wear and cable fatigue highly.
Serious robot companies employ more reinforcement-learning researchers than reliability engineers.
The software must be boring: watchdog processes, safe states, graceful degradation on sensor loss.
Battery endurance, not intelligence, caps most deployments.
config.correction: The ratio runs the other way — more reliability engineers than RL researchers, because hardware dominates the uptime statistics.
config.why: Dust, thermal drift, cable fatigue: the boring constraint outranks the clever model — which is why the software must also be boring.

activities.anchor: embodied AI is just a language model with arms
activities.caption: drag the divider — chatbot physics versus robot physics
activities.name: rbeEmbodiedCompare

config.prompt: Same algorithms, different physics — drag between the two worlds:

before.label: Chatbot intelligence
before.text: Thinks in seconds; the core artefacts are context windows and weights; a bad answer costs a regenerate click.

after.label: Embodied control
after.text: Balance at kilohertz on milliwatt budgets; the core artefacts are control rates, torque limits and state estimators; a dropped object has no undo.

config.why: Language-model intelligence enters as a planner layer above the real-time loop, not instead of it.

activities.anchor: The warehouse is the field's clearest economics case study
activities.caption: run the deployment — divide the labour
activities.name: rbeWarehouseBranch

config.root: You are deploying robots in a fulfilment centre. The economics of embodiment force a division of labour.

choices.label: Robots do transport in mapped, human-free aisles; humans pick from clutter
Robots also pick arbitrary objects from clutter
Redesign the environment around the robots' weaknesses

kiva.text: Transport is flat, mapped and repetitive; manipulation is the hard part — exactly the locomotion-versus-dexterity split the research frontier predicts. This is why the successful deployments share it.

dexterity.text: General-purpose manipulation is unsolved: contact dynamics are discontinuous (a fingertip either slips or grips), and tactile sensing lags vision by decades.

redesign.text: Embodiment scales where the environment can be redesigned around the robot's weaknesses — and stalls where it cannot, which is why the general-purpose home robot remains a venture-funding category rather than a product category.

config.why: Value per movement and tolerance for chaos decide where robots work — and the boring constraint underneath is energy: runtime, not intelligence, caps most deployments.
